title: The burden on Hadrach, Damascus, Tyre and Philistia (Zech 9:1–8)
speaker: The LORD (through the prophet)
description: The word of the LORD rests on Hadrach and Damascus, Hamath, Tyre and Sidon; Tyre, though rich and fortified, will be burned; Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and Ashdod will be humbled and a remnant of Philistia will belong to God like a clan in Judah; the LORD will encamp about his house so that no oppressor passes through again.
in_text_interpretation: No agent of the judgment is named.

interpretations.label: Predicts Alexander's march through Syria, Phoenicia and Philistia (333–332 BC)
proponents: E. W. Hengstenberg (as quoted by Keil)
C. F. Keil (1868), as the "commencement" of fulfilment with Koehler
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the cities are named in the order of Alexander's advance after Issus. Historical evidence: Parmenio seized Damascus; Tyre fell in 332 after a long siege; Gaza was stormed (Arrian; Josephus). Objection (Koehler, via Keil): the conversion of the Philistine remnant (9:7) was not fulfilled by Alexander, so Keil treats his campaign only as the beginning of a longer fulfilment.

referents.symbol: The unnamed destroyer of Tyre and Philistia

interpretations.label: Written in 333 BC, just after Issus, as Alexander advanced
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Tyre is described as never yet taken, as it had not been when Alexander attacked it; 9:8 is an interpolation by a reader who knew the story that Alexander spared Jerusalem (cf. Josephus, Ant. 11.8.5). The first part was "fulfilled in a measure" when Alexander took the cities.
